title: A 132-to-148GHz CMOS 4TX-4RX FMCW Radar Transceiver Array with Cavity-Backed Antenna-in-Package Achieving 28dBm EIRP
problem: D-band (132-148GHz) FMCW radar transceivers are limited by low output power from frequency multipliers and power amplifiers, low on-chip antenna gain, and small array sizes, resulting in insufficient EIRP (<11.6 dBm) for high-resolution imaging and long-range detection.
motivation: D-band spectrum offers large available bandwidth for future high-resolution radars and high-data-rate wireless; compensating for substantial free-space loss requires high EIRP but is constrained by process fMAx and breakdown voltage limitations.
method: The chip has four transmit and four receive channels. It generates D-band signals using a frequency quadrupler (a circuit that multiplies the signal frequency by 4 and amplifies it), then amplifies them further with a power amplifier built from low-loss slow-wave coplanar waveguide (special interconnects designed to reduce signal loss) and LC-ladder power combiners (circuits that merge multiple signals into a single stronger output). Finally, it uses an antenna integrated into the chip package with a cavity backing (which focuses the radiation to boost antenna gain). Together, these components achieve 28.7 dBm EIRP (effective radiated power).
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining a cavity-backed antenna integrated into the chip package with LC-ladder power-combining circuits to achieve 28.7 dBm EIRP for D-band radar transceiver arrays.
contributions: 4TX-4RX CMOS D-band FMCW radar transceiver array
High-power amplitude-phase harmonic modulated frequency quadrupler
Low-loss slow-wave CPW and LC-ladder power-combiner for PA efficiency
primary_theme: High-EIRP D-band FMCW radar transceiver array
